texts: mixed: the rule fires and every participant is covered, but the silken threads are filed under the role for things an action creates or changes, when leaving them on the lantern moves them unchanged — so a question about what the moth left behind can miss them. That is a slip on the translator's side, not in your wording: the sentence is already in the shape that parses best (one finite clause per event, participants introduced in the when-clause and referred back to afterwards), so keep it as it is.

mixed: same picture — the whenever rule fires, "is resting" is anchored properly and "onto the lantern" is kept as the destination, but the shed threads again take the create/change role instead of the moved-unchanged one. Nothing in your wording causes it, so no rewrite is needed.

mixed: the universal is captured as a rule over every silken thread, with the underside recorded as part of a nightmoth, but the moth came out here under the symbol night_moth while your first two sentences produced nightmoth, so these facts sit under two unconnected symbols. Use one hyphenated spelling throughout: "Every silken thread comes from the underside of a night-moth."
